The product

Meet the Mindathon game

A real, physical game — designed, built and played hands-on.

What Is Mindathon?

Challenges. Thinking. Responding.

Mindathon presents cognitive challenges that players must think through and respond to — using their memory, focus, speed and reasoning.

Because it is a physical game, everyone plays together in the same room. No phones, no screens, no autoplay — just active participation.

  • Think first, respond fast — challenges reward attention and accuracy.
  • Play together — built for families, classrooms and groups.
  • Made by an experienced memory trainer — 33 years of training expertise.
What Do You Actually Do?

What playing Mindathon feels like

Fully present

Every round demands attention — there is no background mode.

Playfully fast

Rounds move at a pace that keeps thinking sharp and energy high.

Social by nature

Players encourage, react and celebrate together as they play.

Rewarding

Getting a challenge right feels earned — effort turns into small wins.

How You Play

Four steps, one game

Mindathon is designed to be understood quickly — the same simple flow behind every challenge.

01

Choose a challenge

A host picks a challenge and explains it in seconds.

02

Think

Players use memory, focus and reasoning to work out the answer.

03

Play & respond

Hands, voice, full attention — everyone responds and takes part.

04

Practise & improve

Next challenge, again and again — practice is how skills grow.

Keep it simple

No rules overload. Just play.

Mindathon is designed to be understood quickly. A host explains each challenge, everyone plays a round, and the next challenge begins.

  • Easy to start — learn each challenge in seconds.
  • Variety keeps it fresh — different challenges, different skills.
  • Works in groups — family, classroom or training centre.
What It Trains

Designed to practise six cognitive areas

Each area below describes a cognitive skill and how Mindathon provides opportunities to practise it. No shortcuts, no promises — just structured, regular practice through play.

Memory & Recall

Memory is the ability to hold information and bring it back when needed. Mindathon challenges give players opportunities to observe, remember and recall — sometimes under time pressure, sometimes after a distraction.

How Mindathon supports it: challenges that ask players to remember what they saw, heard or did — and use it correctly a moment later.

Focus & Attention

Focus means directing attention to one thing and keeping it there. Mindathon rounds are structured so that every challenge begins and ends — players must be present from the first moment to the last.

How Mindathon supports it: short, well-defined challenges that reward attention, with gameplay that discourages drifting.

Problem Solving

Problem solving is working through a question or situation to reach an answer. Mindathon challenges present problems that cannot be solved by reflex alone — they ask players to reason, compare and decide.

How Mindathon supports it: challenges with rules and constraints that require thought before responding.

Mental Speed & Accuracy

Mental speed is how quickly the mind processes information; accuracy is getting it right. Mindathon gives players the chance to practise both — responding quickly while keeping answers correct.

How Mindathon supports it: timed and paced challenges that balance speed against getting it right.

Mental Flexibility

Mental flexibility is the ability to switch between ideas, rules or approaches. Mindathon keeps things varied — the rules of one challenge may not apply to the next, so players learn to adapt.

How Mindathon supports it: rotating challenge types that require players to change strategy from round to round.

Confidence & Positive Attitude

Trying something new takes confidence. Mindathon creates a supportive environment where players are encouraged to respond, learn from mistakes and try again — building a positive attitude toward challenges.

How Mindathon supports it: a play format where every player participates, and every attempt is part of learning.

Why It's Different

Active participation changes the experience

A physical game. No screens required. Watching a video or tapping a screen keeps the mind mostly passive — Mindathon gets people actively thinking, responding and participating.

Passive learning

You watch, you listen, you absorb — and often, you drift.

Active participation

You think, you respond, you act. Every round engages the mind.

Common questions

Quick answers

Is Mindathon screen-free?
Yes. Mindathon is a physical game — no screens, apps or accounts needed. Players respond with their hands, voice and full attention.
How many people can play?
Mindathon works for individuals and groups — from a family around the table to a classroom. Contact the team for guidance on group sizes and the most suitable version.
Where can Mindathon be used?
At home with family, in classrooms, training centres, community groups — anywhere a group of people can sit together and play.
Who is Mindathon for?
Mindathon is designed for students, families, schools, training centres and educational organisations. For guidance on age suitability, contact the Mindathon team.

Play is the best kind of practice

Bring Mindathon home or to your classroom — and start playing.
